items.title: Product modulo 1,000,000,007
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 1000, then n integers, each from 0 to 10^9. Print their product modulo 1000000007. Multiply in a 64-bit type and reduce after every step. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Sum until the input ends
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read integers until the input ends, with no count given first. Each is between -10^12 and 10^12, and there are at most 10^5 of them. Print their sum. Loop on while (cin >> x). Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Reverse the words of a line
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read one line of up to 10^5 characters: words of lowercase letters separated by one or more spaces. Print the words in reverse order, separated by single spaces. Use getline and a std::string. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Rank by score, then by name
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 10^5, then n lines each holding a name (lowercase letters) and a score (0 to 10^9). Print the names one per line, highest score first, and names in alphabetical order when scores tie. Use a struct and std::sort with a lambda. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Distinct values with sort and unique
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 2*10^5, then n integers. Print how many distinct values there are, then the distinct values in increasing order on one line. Use std::sort, std::unique, and erase. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Every permutation in order
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 6. Print every permutation of 1 to n in lexicographic order, one per line, numbers separated by spaces. Use std::next_permutation. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Range sums with prefix sums
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n and q, each up to 2*10^5, then n integers (absolute value up to 10^9), then q queries l r with 1 <= l <= r <= n. Print the sum of elements l to r for each query, one per line. Build the prefix sums once, with std::partial_sum or a loop, in 64-bit integers. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: cppreference: std::set, std::map, and set::lower_bound
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read the member list and the complexity of insert, erase, find, lower_bound, and upper_bound. multiset is the same page family.

links.label: Saad, Mastering 4 critical SKILLS using C++ 17, section 41: More on STL, 11 lectures, 62 min

items.title: Smallest value at least x
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, then n integers into a std::set. Then read q and q queries x. For each, print the smallest value in the set that is at least x, or -1 if there is none. Use the set's own lower_bound, not std::lower_bound, so each query is O(log n). Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: The most frequent word
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 2*10^5, then n lowercase words. Print the word that appears most often and its count. On a tie, print the alphabetically smallest such word. Count with a std::map<std::string, int>. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Balanced brackets with a stack
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read t, then t strings made of the six bracket characters, each nonempty and up to 10^5 long. For each, print YES if every bracket closes the most recent open one of its kind and none is left open, otherwise NO. Use std::stack. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Cheapest merging with a priority queue
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n, 1 <= n <= 2*10^5, then n positive integers up to 10^9. Merging two numbers costs their sum and leaves the sum in their place. Merge until one number is left, always taking the two smallest, and print the total cost. Use std::priority_queue with std::greater. Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.

items.title: Sliding window maximum with a deque
items.minutesBasis: Proposed
items.what: Read n and k, 1 <= k <= n <= 2*10^5, then n integers. Print the maximum of every window of k consecutive elements, left to right, on one line. Keep indices in a std::deque so the whole run is O(n). Run it here. Compiler Explorer compiles it with gcc 16.2, -O2 -std=c++23, and the page checks the output.
